# UHI — Continuous Morphology Archetypes for Heat Mitigation Across 66 Cities

> Companion code and open data for a peer-reviewed study quantifying how continuous urban
> morphology relates to summer surface urban heat island (SUHI) intensity across 66 cities
> and 15 Köppen climate zones, using harmonised satellite and open building-footprint data.

## Citation

Emekci, S., & Emekci, H. (2026). Beyond local climate zones: Continuous morphology
archetypes for heat mitigation across 66 cities. Sustainable Cities and Society, 150, 107814.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scs.2026.107814

Software and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19897974 (concept DOI, always latest version)
Repository: https://github.com/hemekci/UHI

## What this is

A reproducible pipeline and a harmonised patch-level dataset. Each row is a 1 km² built-up
patch carrying a summer surface-UHI anomaly derived from 3-summer rolling-mean Landsat 8/9
land-surface temperature, plus eight continuous morphology descriptors extracted from open
global building-footprint-with-height products. The design isolates within-city morphology
effects from climate-regime offsets using linear mixed-effects models with a city random
intercept, fitted globally and within each Köppen zone.

## Key facts

- Sample: 33,715 harmonised 1 km² patches; 33,498 retained after a physical-plausibility
  screen (|UHI anomaly| <= 40 °C). 66 cities, 15 Köppen climate zones.
- Per-zone mixed-effects models are fitted for 14 of the 15 zones; Dsa has a single city,
  so a city random intercept is not estimable there.
- Global model: marginal R² = 0.25, conditional R² = 0.39, ICC = 0.18. All eight morphology
  features significant at 95%.
- Tree-canopy fraction is the only universal cooling lever: negative coefficient in all 14
  modelled zones, significant in 13 (standardised beta = -0.64, p < 1e-122).
- Other cooling levers: water fraction (-0.58), 80th-percentile NDVI (-0.31), building-height
  coefficient of variation (-0.18), mean building height (-0.09).
- Warming levers: bare-soil fraction (+0.42), built-up fraction (+0.31).
- Per-zone models raise the patch-weighted pooled marginal R² to 0.38, reaching 0.55 in Dwa.
- 144 Pareto-efficient patches in (UHI, density) space cluster into three archetypes.
- Morphology explains a limited share of SUHI variance; background climate dominates, which
  is consistent with Zhao et al. (2014, Nature) and Manoli et al. (2019, Nature).

## Data files

- data/published/uhi_morphology_patches_v1.parquet — 33,715 rows, 28 columns, full sample
- data/published/uhi_morphology_patches_screened_v1.parquet — 33,498 rows, the modelling sample
- data/published/diagnostics.json — global model coefficients, CIs, R², ICC
- data/published/diagnostics_perzone.json — per-zone coefficients and fit statistics
- data/published/pareto_summary.json — per-zone Pareto counts
- data/published/archetype_cards.json — the three morphology archetypes
- data/published/README.md — full column dictionary and known missing values

## Code

- src/ingest — Earth Engine ingest and city rosters
- src/features — patch features and the quality screen
- src/morphology — building-footprint morphology extraction
- src/model — mixed-effects and XGBoost + SHAP
- src/pareto — empirical Pareto extraction
- src/typology — archetype clustering
- src/metrics — R², ICC, hierarchical diagnostics
- run/conf — Hydra configuration
- run/pipeline — stage entry points, including make_figures.py

## Scope and limitations

The dependent variable is surface UHI from satellite land-surface temperature, not
canopy-layer air temperature and not human thermal comfort. Building-height coverage is
absent for about half the patches, sparsest in the Global South; a height-exclusion
sensitivity analysis shows the conclusions do not depend on the height features.
Coefficients are specific to the 1 km aggregation scale. The analysis is observational, so
coefficients quantify association rather than identified causal effects.
